q: 1. The unit of measurement of long thin work like skirting, handrail, cornice, coping, bedding etc. is
explain: Linear works where the cross-section is uniform and length is the primary measurement are recorded in running metres (per m).

q: 2. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled by
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
earth excavated from far away from the site
explain: If a contractor over-excavates a foundation, they must fill the excess depth with concrete (usually 1:4:8 or as specified) at their own cost to ensure structural stability.

q: 3. The nominal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are
explain: Standard specifications allow for a normal lead (horizontal distance) of 30m and a normal lift (vertical distance) of 1.5m in general earthwork.

q: 4. For electric wiring such as fan, light, plug etc., the estimate is made in terms of
options: total load at main in KW
total length of wiring in metres
explain: Electrical installations in buildings are generally estimated by counting the number of 'points' (each light, fan, or socket outlet is one point).

q: 5. The brick work is measured in sq. metre, in case of
options: half brick walls or the partition
explain: All the mentioned types (honeycomb, soling, and half-brick partitions) are thin or specialized brickworks where area is the standard unit of measurement.

q: 6. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled by
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
the earth excavated from a borrow pit far away from the site
explain: If a contractor over-excavates foundation trenches, they must fill the excess depth with concrete of the same specification as the foundation, at their own cost.

q: 7. The plan of a building is in the form of a rectangle with center line dimensions of outer walls as 9.7 m x 14.7 m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30 m. Then its plinth area is
8. In long and short wall method of estimation, the length of long wall is the centre to centre distance between the walls and
options: one fourth breadth of wall on each side
half breadth of wall on each side
explain: To find the out-to-out length of a long wall, you take the center-to-center distance and add half the width of the wall at each end (Total = C/C + 1 Full Width).

q: 9. The measurement of still grills is taken in terms of
explain: Steel items like grills, gates, and reinforcement bars are measured by weight (kg or quintal).

q: 10. In the case of roof truss made of steel, rivets, bolts, and nuts usually account for
explain: An allowance of 5% of the total weight of the steel members is usually added to account for connecting rivets, bolts, and nuts.

q: 11. Whenever the whitewashing or distempering is done on corrugated iron sheets, in the estimation the plan area of that sheets is increased by
explain: Corrugated iron (CI) sheets have a larger actual surface area than their flat plan area; a 14% increase is typically allowed for painting/whitewashing.

q: 12. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement (C), steel (S) and coarse aggregate (A) in the decreasing order.
explain: Steel (~7850 kg/m³) > Cement (~1440 kg/m³) > Coarse Aggregate (~1200-1400 kg/m³) > Wood (~600-800 kg/m³). Note: Answer key indicates option B, but scientifically Steel is heaviest.

q: 13. Unit of measurement of supply of brick is
explain: Bricks are manufactured as individual units and are supplied, counted, and paid for by number (usually per 1000 units).

q: 14. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per metre length is equal to
explain: The weight is calculated using the formula d²/162. So, (10 * 10) / 162 = 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62 kg.

q: 15. The most reliable estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate is prepared based on actual measurements from drawings and is therefore the most accurate and reliable.

q: 16. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: A revised estimate must be prepared if the actual expenditure or the probable cost exceeds the sanctioned amount by more than 5%.

q: 17. The plinth area of a building includes
options: area of walls at floor level
explain: While internal areas like walls and lifts are part of the built-up area, common estimation rules often distinguish what constitutes 'Plinth' vs 'Carpet'. The key indicates cantilevered porches (if covered) are often included.

q: 18. Carpet area does not include the area of
explain: Carpet area is the actual usable area where a carpet can be laid. It excludes walls, balconies, toilets, kitchens, and corridors.

q: 19. The floor area includes the area of the balcony up to
explain: In many building bylaws, only 50% of the balcony area is counted towards the total floor area or Floor Space Index (FSI).

q: 20. The area of the segmental portion of an arch with span l and riser r is approximately given by
explain: The area of a parabolic or shallow segmental arch is roughly calculated as two-thirds of the product of the span and the rise (2/3 × l × r).

q: 21. The measurement is not made in square metres in case of
explain: RCC Chhajjas (projections) are often measured in cubic metres or as a specific item, whereas DPC and formwork are strictly square metre items.

q: 22. The measurement is made for stone work in square metre in case of
explain: Thin stone veneer or wall facing is measured in m², whereas massive stone structures like columns are in m³; however, combined options often point to area-based cladding.

q: 23. The damp proof course (DPC) is measured in
explain: DPC is a thin layer applied over the plinth; since its thickness is very small and specified, it is measured by area (m²).

q: 24. The rate of an item of work depends on
explain: The unit rate is influenced by the quality of materials (specs), the mix ratio (proportion), and how the work is performed (method).

q: 25. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
explain: The Prismoidal rule (Simpson's rule for volume) states V = D/3 [First + Last + 4(Sum of even areas) + 2(Sum of odd areas)].

q: 26. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: This is the general formula for the cross-sectional area of a road on side-sloping ground where 'r' is the ground slope and 's' is the side slope.

q: 27. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are horizontal ledges left between the top of the cutting and the toe of the bank to improve stability and prevent siltation.

q: 28. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
explain: Shallow works like surface dressing (cleaning) and surface excavation (up to 30cm) are paid by area (m²) rather than volume.

q: 29. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: This formula represents the area of a trapezoidal cross-section in an embankment (banking) when the original ground has a transverse slope 'r' and the side slopes are 's'.

q: 30. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. When depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm. is
explain: When the depth of excavation is shallow (less than 30 cm), it is treated as 'Surface Excavation' and measured in square meters (sq m) rather than volume.

q: 31. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting and end points of the curves
explain: Standard highway surveying requires cross-sections at regular intervals (usually 30m), at critical curve points, and always perpendicular to the center line for accurate volume calculation.

q: 32. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc. up to 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/ hard rock is in
explain: Small trenching for utilities (pipes/cables) at standardized depths is frequently paid per linear meter.

q: 33. The unit of payment for A.C. sheet roofing is in
explain: Sheet roofing (Asbestos Cement, GI, or tiles) is measured based on the superficial area covered, hence square meters (sq. m.).

q: 34. In a detailed estimate the provision for contingencies is usually
explain: Contingencies are incidental expenses of a miscellaneous character which cannot be reasonably predicted; 3% to 5% of the total estimate is reserved for this.

q: 35. Revised estimate is warranted when the sanctions estimate exceeds, for whether reason, by more than
explain: Administrative and technical rules dictate that if the expenditure on a work is likely to exceed the original sanctioned amount by more than 5%, a revised estimate must be submitted for approval.

q: 36. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: Standard AC corrugated sheets are manufactured with a width of 1.05 meters to allow for overlaps during installation.

q: 37. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is a forward-looking financial plan that estimates income and expenses for a specific period, usually one year.

q: 38. Center line method of estimation is mostly used for:
explain: The center line method is a quick and accurate way to calculate quantities for walls and foundations in rectangular or circular buildings.

q: 39. 'Bill of Quantities' are prepared by .....
explain: Quantity Surveyors (QS) are the professionals specialized in managing all costs relating to building and civil engineering projects, including the preparation of the BOQ.

q: 40. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling provides a hard, stable base for the foundation concrete, especially when the underlying soil is soft or has low bearing capacity.

q: 41. A work costing more than Rs. one core is termed as
explain: High-value projects (typically exceeding a specific threshold like 1 Crore) are classified as Major Works requiring higher-level technical and administrative sanction.

q: 42. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Thin walls (thickness < 10cm or half-brick) and decorative honey-comb brickwork are measured by superficial area (m²) rather than volume.

q: 43. In the center line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the center line length at each junction?
explain: At each 'T' junction, a length equal to half the breadth of the wall is deducted from the total center line length to avoid double counting the corners.

q: 44. In long and short wall method of estimation, the length of long wall is the center to center distance between the walls and
options: half breadth of wall on each side
one fourth breadth of wall on each side
explain: Length of long wall = (c/c distance) + (2 * half breadth) = c/c distance + full breadth of wall.

q: 45. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc, upto 1.5m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: As noted previously for utility trenching, the standard unit of payment is often the linear meter for specific depth ranges.

q: 46. The unit of measurement of masonry work (ashlar and rubble) is
explain: Stone masonry, whether ashlar (dressed) or rubble (undressed), is a volumetric item measured in cubic meters (m³).

q: 47. A fixed stated sum of penalty to help by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-estimated sum agreed upon in the contract to be paid if the contractor fails to complete the work on time.

q: 48. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Items like rolling shutters and steel doors are typically measured by their clear area in square meters (m²).

q: 49. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate, is
options: Location of site and local labour charges
explain: A detailed estimate must account for physical quantities as well as logistical factors like material transport and regional labor rates.

q: 50. The number of corrugations in a galvanized corrugated sheet usually
explain: The most common configuration for standard commercial GI roofing sheets is 10 corrugations per sheet width.

q: 51. In standard notation which of the following is prismoidal formula for earthwork calculations
explain: The prismoidal formula (Simpson's Rule) for volume between two sections with a mid-section area $A_m$ is $V =  rac{L}{6}(A_1 + 4A_m + A_2)$.

q: 52. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: By definition, 1 Hectare is the area of a square with 100m sides: $100 	imes 100 = 10,000 	ext{ m}^2$.

q: 53. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D/3 [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (also known as Simpson's rule for volume) uses the coefficients 1, 4, 2, 4... 1. It is expressed as $V = \frac{D}{3} [A_1 + A_n + 4(\text{even areas}) + 2(\text{remaining odd areas})]$.

q: 54. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate must account for the volume of material, its market availability, and the cost to transport it to the site (lead charges).

q: 55. The size of the standard modular brick is
explain: The actual size of a modular brick is 19 x 9 x 9 cm. When mortar joints (1 cm) are added, the nominal size becomes 20 x 10 x 10 cm.

q: 56. Whenever the whitewashing or distempering is done on corrugated iron sheets, in the estimation the plan area the sheets is increased by
explain: Because of the 'waves' in corrugated sheets, the actual surface area is greater than the plan area. For standard GI sheets, a 14% increase is applied.

q: 57. In case of steel rolling shutters, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: Rolling shutters have a corrugated profile. To estimate the painting area for one side, the flat area is multiplied by 1.1 or 1.25 (1 1/4) depending on the corrugation depth.

q: 58. The supply of paint, varnish and enamel is measured in ............
explain: Liquid finishing materials like paints, varnishes, and enamels are commercially supplied and estimated in liters (ltr).

q: 59. The unit of measurement of aluminium partition is ............
explain: Aluminum partitions are measured by the area they cover, which is calculated in square meters (m2).

q: 60. The unit of measurement of site clearance in irrigation canal is ............
explain: Large scale site clearance involving earthwork volumes in canal construction is often measured in cubic meters (m3), though surface clearance is sometimes m2.

q: 61. The quantity for expansion joint in building is worked out in ............
explain: Expansion joints are typically measured by their length in running meters (m).

q: 62. The unit measurement of R.C.C. works in shelves of jail (thickness and type specified) is .........
explain: Thin R.C.C. members like shelves or fins with a specified thickness are measured in m2.

q: 63. The unit of measurement of welding and soldering of plates is ............
explain: Welding and soldering are measured by the linear length of the joint, which is per meter (per m).but as per key quintal

q: 64. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for ............
explain: According to IS 1200, no deductions are made for ends of beams, rafters, or small openings less than 0.5 m2 when calculating plastering area.
